en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Twentieth Chapter
On Animal Discourse:
Is there such a thing as being born among animals in the realms of the devas?
Yes, there is.
Is there such a thing as a "deva" among the animals?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is there such a thing as an "animal" among the devas?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the world of the gods the animal realm?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
"Are there animals among the devas?
"Yes.
"Are there therein beetles, moths, mosquitoes, flies, snakes, scorpions, centipedes, and spiders?"
It should not be said so… [as before] …Is it not the case that there are no animals among the devas?
Yes, it is.
"Is it not the case that there is there an elephant named Erāvaṇa, a divine vehicle yoked with a thousand [beings]?
"Yes.
"If indeed there is there an elephant named Erāvaṇa, a divine vehicle yoked with a thousand, then surely, O sir, you should say:"
“There are animals among the devas.
Are there animals among the devas? Yes.
Are there there elephant-keepers, horse-keepers, fodder-gatherers, jailers, and cooks?
One should not say so.
Therefore, it follows that there are no animals among the devas.
The Discussion on Animal Talk is finished.
